section: Lucy Letby - Cross-examination by Nick Johnson KC

blocks.text: 2 June 2023
Lucy Letby - Cross-examination Day 6: Babies I, J & K
CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)
Friday, 2 June 2023
(In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON (continued)

Thank you all, members of the jury, very much for making yourselves available to continue with the trial today. As I said to you, we will have a reasonable session now, then we'll have a slightly longer break this afternoon, then finish at around the usual time, certainly by 4 o'clock. All right?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, Mr Johnson.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It has been, I think, 8 days since you were last sitting there. In those days have you thought of anything that you have said so far that you would like to alter or review?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I would like to move on, if we may, to the third incident involving [Baby I]. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This happened towards the end of the night shift of the 13th into 14 October 2015. All right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Have you got your defence statement there? I think it's just there under the iPad. You deal with [Baby I] at page 14. You can see that at paragraph 113 you deal with 30 September. At paragraph 115 on page 15 you deal with the incident that we have
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: just dealt with, which is what happened in nursery 2 in the early hours of 13 October.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: With me so far?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you don't mention at all -- before you get to -- at paragraph 119, which is [Baby I]'s final collapse and death, you don't mention at all the incident on 14 October.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When you were asked questions by your counsel on 15 May, you said that you had no recollection of what happened on this shift or of [Baby I]'s desaturation; do you remember saying that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was that the truth?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it your case that the staffing levels on this shift caused or contributed to the life-threatening desaturation suffered by [Baby I] on 14 October?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it your case that medical competence or incompetence contributed in any way?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is it your case that anybody's mistakes made a contribution to [Baby I]'s desaturation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we go to the [Baby I] sequence, please, Mr Murphy, it's sequence number 3, and could we go to tile 7. Click on that, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This gives us the layout, doesn't it? Can you see that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You see that you were one-to-one with [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Joanne Williams, with two other children, that were also in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Nursery 2, Laura Eagles looking after two, who included [Baby G]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Janet Cox in nursery 4 with a single child?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then some other babies whose location cannot be confirmed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Should we take it though, that given that Janet Cox was looking after three of those other babies, they are likely to have been either in nursery 3 or nursery 4?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is there any inference we can draw, so far as the other three babies are concerned, who were being looked after by Caroline Oakley and Laura Eagles?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I couldn't say.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Okay. If we go to tile 46, please. This concerns an examination by Dr Neame very early in the shift at 22.05.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It shows that [Baby I] was stable, pink, settled and had good chest movement, albeit she was on a ventilator. Do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't remember the shift specifically, but yes, I agree that's written there, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Well, you've heard the evidence relating to all this, haven't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you agree that by 1 o'clock the following morning on 14 October, [Baby I] was improving?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'd have to review the notes again. I can't say from my memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We'll look at your note then at tile 60, please. We can see at the top -- this is the note that you made towards the beginning of the shift; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we scroll down, please, do we see a note that you made at the end of the shift at 08.43?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We can see that you have recorded the fact that the blood gas at 01.00, which is why I have selected that time, was good?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: No changes had been made to the ventilator?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Temperature elevated, incubator temperature reduced; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And other signs were good at that stage, would you agree?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So, for example:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "[Baby I] tolerating handling better. Tone appears improved. Remains pale. Abdomen distended but soft. Nil obtained from the NG tube"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you have then made a note, haven't you, of events at 05.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just tell us what you have noted there.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "At 05.00, abdomen noted to be more distended and firmer in appearance with area of discolouration spreading on righthand side. Veins more prominent. Oxygen requirement began to increase, colour became pale. Reviewed by Reg Neame. Ventilation increased to CMV, rate 70, 30/6, gradually requiring 100% oxygen. Blood gases poor as charted. Clear air entry, slightly reduced on left. Chest movement reduced. Nil obtained from NG tube throughout. Continued to decline. Re-intubated at approximately 07.00. Initially responded well. Consultant Jayaram aware and on way to unit. Abdomen firm and distended. Overall colour pale. X-rays carried out. Resuscitation commenced as documented in medical notes. Night and day staff members present. Drugs as documented given via peripheral line. Ciprofloxacin stopped to allow access therefore only half dose completed. Morphine increased to 40 micrograms per kilogram per hour and dobutamine increased to 20 micrograms per kilo per [hour]. [Baby I] placed back onto ventilator and care handed over to Staff Nurse Tomlins [as read]."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Please describe for us the discolouration that you saw.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall that from my memory now.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But it was moving discolouration?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't believe it was moving.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, what does the word "spreading" mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That the area was getting bigger, not that it was actively moving. The discolouration was becoming bigger in size.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So do you remember it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, but that's how I read my own note to be.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where did you get the time of 5 o'clock from?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Had you ever seen this sort of spreading discolouration before?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't comment because I don't remember it right now.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Don't or won't?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't remember it.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where did you get the time of 5 o'clock from?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know. I don't know if it's from paper charts, I'm not sure from my memory.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, I'm going to suggest to you that if you really had seen this at 05.00 hours, as you have recorded, you would have escalated it straightaway. Do you agree with that or not?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't comment on what time the doctor did come. It does say I've asked for a review. I'm not sure without looking at the notes when that happened.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What had happened about 24 hours earlier?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know what you mean, sorry. With [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I think you know who I'm talking about, don't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't understand the question that you're asking me.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What had happened to [Baby I] about 24 hours earlier?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: She'd been found in the cot.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: In what state?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Apnoeic.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Oh, come on. She wasn't apnoeic --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Gasping.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Almost dead. Do you agree?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. So this child, who had been almost dead 24 hours earlier, according to your note, has now got a more distended and firm abdomen. Is that a positive or a negative sign?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Negative.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: She has discolouration which is spreading on her righthand side. Is that a positive or negative sign?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Negative.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So what would you have done if what you wrote was true?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I would have escalated it to somebody, either a senior nurse or a doctor.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But we know what time Dr Neame attended, don't we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't know from my memory now.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's go to tile 79:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Asked to see patient re increased requirement for oxygen..."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "... and decreased saturations"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where is there mention to the doctor of discolouration?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't see that there until further down into the text.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, where do you see it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Abdomen distended and mottled."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Any evidence of moving discolouration?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Whose responsibility was it to communicate to Dr Neame the issue that you have recorded in your notes as having occurred at 5 o'clock?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Mine.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You didn't communicate it, did you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't say specifically what time I asked Dr Neame to come. He obviously has come at 5.55, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Is what you have recorded in your nursing note a serious event?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's showing a decline, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Oh, but let's look at the context of this decline.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: A child that had almost died 24 hours earlier; correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Abdomen more distended and firmer. Area of discolouration spreading on right-hand side. Veins more prominent. Oxygen requirement beginning to increase.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Colour became pale."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: All your note?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This would have been an emergency, wouldn't it, if what you wrote was true?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't believe it was an emergency. It was showing a decline, yes, and I'm not sure who I escalated it to and when.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This is another example, isn't it, Lucy Letby, of you writing a nursing note that creates the impression of a more gradual decline than in fact really happened?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I don't agree.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You sabotaged [Baby I] at about 6 o'clock, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest to you that Dr Neame was called at about 5.50; okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we go to page 78, I'll show you the reason why and you can comment. If we go back to tile 78, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There we can see, in the third column of infusions, an infusion of morphine sulphate being given to [Baby I] at about 5.50, prescribed by Dr Neame --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- with your signature underneath.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And this goes with his note, doesn't it, that I've just shown you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And this is the time he arrived, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: From that, I can't say what time he prescribed it, but yes, the infusion was commenced at 5.50, so it would have been prescribed prior to that, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. Go back to tile 75 though, please -- sorry, tile 76, I beg your pardon. Down to the bottom, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm afraid this is one of the ones where we may have to select part of the -- thank you. Scroll up, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We see your initials, don't we, at 01.00 hours, down to 07.00 hours?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We also see under the 5 o'clock column your handwriting, don't we --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: -- in that large left-hand column? Does it read "metronidazole"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Does it also read:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "05.30, abdo distended ++"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why is there such a difference between your nursing note and what you have written in handwriting there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The nursing note was reflecting a period from 5 o'clock when her observations started to change.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What was it about the observations that started to change at 5 o'clock?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: She was needing an increase in oxygen and her abdomen was obviously becoming distended at about 05.30.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where do we see the increase in oxygen on this document?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: On the chart there she's gone from 60% to, between 5 and 6, 100%.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where is that, sorry?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: On the FiO2 column. I can't... Does the mouse...?
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: That doesn't work, sorry.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's on the left-hand column where the two ticks are.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where it goes to 100%?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Which column is that in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: 6 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes, not the 5 o'clock column, is it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. But by 6 o'clock, that was her oxygen requirement.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can you see -- just where the cursor is now, do you see it, where it's pointing to a 60?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can you see that you have written in something above that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Squeaky", yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes. What does "squeaky" mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Air entry, so the ticks there are for left and rightsided chest movement and air entry and I've said it's squeaky and that's led me to then do suction.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What does squeaky mean?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Squeaky means you haven't got clear -- when doctors and nurses write "clear entry", you don't hear anything, but to hear a squeak means you're not getting full lung expansion.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's look at that then. At 5 o'clock, according to you, you've got a child who was almost dead 24 hours earlier; correct?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: A child whose abdomen has expanded and is becoming harder; yes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes, at 05.30, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: 5 o'clock according to your nursing note, but okay, 5.30 here. A child with moving discolouration or spreading discolouration; yes?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Who's on a ventilator and has got squeaky air entry?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you didn't escalate it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Squeaky air entry is not an emergency. The next thing we were going to do is suction, which is what I've gone on to do. We wouldn't be putting out an emergency call for a squeaky air entry.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: But were not restricting ourselves to a squeaky air entry on what you have recorded, are we?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We've got an expanding hardening abdomen and expanding discolouration.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. I can't say now at what time I've bleeped the doctors, I don't know, or who I escalated it to.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: "Asked to see patient" isn't a very urgent request, is it? It's not crash called or bleeped.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's a bleep, yes, because there's no other way of asking the doctor to review them. I don't think that warranted a crash call, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Just think about that: are you seriously suggesting that other than a bleep there is no way to ask a doctor a question or to review a patient?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Unless they're on the unit.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Well, let's think back to [Baby E] and your evidence about [Baby E], the mucky aspirate.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What did you tell the jury was the way of communicating with the doctor on that occasion?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Telephone.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: But the telephone comes from a bleep. I can't -- the only way nurses can speak to a doctor is by bleeping them first. There's no way I can just pick up the phone and say, "Can I speak to..." It has to go through the bleep system.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why don't you mention the discolouration on this manuscript note?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know, I can't answer that.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You took the word squeaky from Dr Neame's note at 5.55, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't agree, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let's look at his note. Go back to his note, please, Mr Murphy, it's tile 79:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "On my arrival Neopuffing. Some chest wall movement. Positive capnograph change. Equal air entry. Some squeaky sounds."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So like you copied Dr Beebe's note in relation -- on 30 September, from an examination at 11.40, here you have done the same, haven't you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, I disagree.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember Dr Neame saying that the mottling he saw, that he has recorded there, "Abdomen distended and mottled", was unusual?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Did you see anything unusual?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can't recall specifically.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Go to tile 85 and go to the report of Dr Wright, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you see that there Dr Wright has recorded the fact that the degree of gaseous distension of the bowel has increased since the previous image of 13 October?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Baby I] had been on a ventilator since then, hadn't she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And the tube goes directly into the lungs, so it doesn't go into the stomach or via the stomach into the bowel, does it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's because you had injected [Baby I] with air, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Baby I] had been nil by mouth, hadn't she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: By the end of your shift, if we go to tile 129, everything had been decompressed, hadn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, I've misread it. It says:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "No significant change in the degree of bowel distension since the previous image earlier in the day."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You had inflated [Baby I] with air, hadn't you, Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: [Baby I] collapsed again at 7 o'clock, didn't she?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: This is one of those cases when air was going in and out of her, but she was not oxygenating; do you remember that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we look at your -- so that's at 7 o'clock, and if anybody needs the reference for that it's in Dr Neame's note at tile 106. If we see your note, it's at 105, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think you read us through it before. Just to remind you, we've got that final paragraph and just above it, it says, about three lines up:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Re-intubated at approximately 7 o'clock."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Have you got that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And by this stage, "Abdomen firm and distended"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That is because you were sabotaging her, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Look at tile 130, please. You record the resuscitation with both the night staff and the day staff present; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: The drugs being given to [Baby I]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And the fact that care was handed over to Shelley Tomlins?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And none of that you now remember?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Not with clear detail, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY
